context: In Part I, we have built a generic construction of web models, based on strong and absolute PCMs. It unifies various models of the literature. In Part II, we have described a theory of Taylor expansion in categories enriched over PCMs. Web models given by our generic construction feature such Taylor expansion as proved in Section 7. Thus, Taylor expansion is compatible with the computational properties described by partial sums, such as determinism, finite or countable non-determinism, randomness, and absolute convergence. Future work. We conjecture that the exponential of our web models is always Lafont (see Remark 25). Our theory of coherent Taylor expansion captures a wide class of web models, but there are no known web-free examples. We conjecture that the analytic version [26] of the category of convenient vector spaces [4] is not a representable PCM category but features a coherent Taylor expansion. Finally, although we described our web models with a strong emphasis on the algebraic point of view of partial sums, it should be possible to adopt a topological viewpoint on absolute PCMs, as it is done in Köthe spaces [12] and finiteness spaces [13].
